lead: Cases Barates from 1929 and a renewed neighbourhood, with a museum in former homes.
text: The Cases Barates (low-cost houses) were built in 1929 as subsidised rental housing for workers in the factories of the industrial estate, and they are an example of popular architecture from the early 20th century. The 2003 redevelopment demolished 784 houses and built new blocks with 754 flats, and the arrival of the metro in 2010 gave the neighbourhood a new boost.

It is divided into three zones: La Estadella, the newest, the Cases Barates, the oldest, and the industrial estate, home to the La Maquinista shopping centre and the former Can Sala factory. Since 2023, the MUHBA Bon Pastor, a municipal museum, has occupied about ten of the former Cases Barates. At 1.87 km², it is one of the largest neighbourhoods in the district.
housing: New blocks from the 2003 redevelopment and the Cases Barates that have been preserved.
